text: Write a program demonstrating that `String` methods do not modify the string. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: ___;                                  // call the method, ignore the result
explanation: Verified: it prints abc then ABC. `toUpperCase` returns a new string and changes nothing, so a call whose result is discarded does nothing at all — and the compiler does not warn, because discarding a return value is legal. This is among the most common beginner errors in Java and it survives into professional code with `trim`, `replace` and `substring`. Chapter 20 explains why immutability is worth this trap.
